messages:
max_ops: heads-up: us-west-2 GPU fleet saw ~25% of new nodes fail provisioning this morning, warm-pool dipped to 72%. Errors show `keystore: decrypt: AccessDenied` and intermittent 502s from keystore-proxy.

tara_infra: any network changes in the region? NAT or firewall rollout?

max_ops: we did push a ruleset to add inline IPS/inspection for outbound flows to third-party telemetry (rolled 03:40 UTC). Failures start ~03:45.

nina_sre: sample node log: ```
2026-04-02T03:46:12Z node-agent error keystore.Decrypt AccessDenied principal=arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/warmup-provisioner req=xyz
2026-04-02T03:46:12Z http: upstream returned 502 from keystore-proxy id=kp-22 req=xyz
```

own_security: I rolled the IPS config to block known bad telemetry hosts; shouldn't touch internal keystore. But IPS does do TLS reassembly for inspection which can drop client cert info.

max_ops: that matches: when client cert is stripped the proxy sometimes responds 403 (unauth), and sometimes 502 if the TLS reassembly fails mid-request. that explains mixed status codes and the audit gaps.

tara_infra: immediate fix: disable TLS reassembly for the keystore destination or add an explicit allow for `keystore.internal:443` in the IPS policy. Which is faster?

own_security: I can add an allow rule now. Proposed rule: `allow tls host:keystore.internal exempt-inspection comment:"keystore bootstrap bypass"`

deploy-bot: security action: inserted IPS allow rule in us-west-2 (ruleset v2026.04.02.11). Propagating to edges (expected 70s).

max_ops: rolling warm-pool rejoin now. watching logs.

nina_sre: seeing retries succeed. warm pool 72% -> 94% in 6m. still a few noisy nodes with repeated connects, marking them for manual reprovision.

own_security: follow-ups: we'll add a test case to our change-validation that runs a keystore mutual-TLS handshake through the IPS appliance in staging before any production rollout. Also updating change playbook to include eng-sre notification for inspection/IPS changes.

tara_infra: infra items: add ephemeral port range increase and pre-scale NAT if warm-pool target > X nodes in a single AZ to avoid port exhaustion during retries. Cost tradeoff?

max_ops: cost note: pre-scaling NAT adds ~$80/day per extra natgw in region. But rolling failures and manual reprovisioning are more expensive operationally. Let's add a quick calc to incident follow-up.

nina_sre: audit observation: KMS CloudTrail shows missing records for ~45s window while IPS was warming up. We should record that as an evidence gap; security ticket SC-812 filed.

own_security: SC-812 created; plan to exempt keystore paths permanently unless we have a validated inspection workflow. Also will request deeper telemetry for the IPS to surface dropped client cert events.

max_ops: action items I'm taking: (1) add keystore-exempt allow in IPS policy (done), (2) create preflight test for any inspection change, (3) run cost calc for NAT pre-scale and add as runbook appendix.

tara_infra: uploading pcap + agent logs to s3://infra-dumps/us-west2/1768888888/pcap.tar.gz

deploy-bot: upload complete: s3://infra-dumps/us-west2/1768888888/pcap.tar.gz

nina_sre: scheduling 1hr postmortem doc and assigning owners for fixes. Thanks for quick turn. :white_check_mark:
